intro_html: Balsamic vinegar does something to beef that salt alone cannot. It cuts the richness, it caramelizes into the gravy over a long cook, and it turns a plain chuck roast into something sweet, tangy, and a little bit fancy for the price of a bottle of vinegar. Each bowl carries 38 grams of protein and 665 calories for about $5.34 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $5.34 a bowl (at everyday cost). Seven ingredients, most of them already in your kitchen, and the only one you might not own keeps for years once you buy it.
shop_smart: Store brand balsamic vinegar is the right buy here. Expensive aged balsamic is meant to be drizzled cold, and eight hours in a slow cooker erases everything you paid extra for.
Chuck roast is the cut. The vinegar and the long braise handle the toughness, so paying up for a tender cut is money set on fire.
Dried oregano and basil are the seasoning, and jars of both last a year. Buy the larger jars if you cook Italian anything, because the small ones cost far more per ounce.
You only need one onion. Buy the bag anyway if the price per pound is better, since onions keep for weeks and every recipe in this section wants them.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry and season it hard with salt, black pepper, oregano, and basil.
Sear it in the vegetable oil over high heat until it is browned on every side, then move it to the slow cooker.
Chop the onion and mince the garlic and scatter them over and around the roast.
Whisk the balsamic vinegar with the olive oil and pour it over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the roast falls apart under a fork.
Shred the beef in the cooker and stir it through the balsamic gravy, letting it sit 10 minutes so the meat drinks some back up.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain so the vinegar has something to land on.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of shredded beef and gravy into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Each bowl lands at 665 calories with 38 grams of protein.

steps: Season the chuck roast with salt, pepper, oregano, and basil.
Sear it in vegetable oil until browned on all sides, then move it to the slow cooker.
Add chopped onion and garlic, then pour over the balsamic vinegar whisked with olive oil.
Cook on low 8 hours until the roast falls apart.
Shred the beef into the gravy, cook the rice, and portion into 14 containers.
